metadata.note: The Cincinnati Northern and its predecessors, Franklin, Ohio - Van Wert - Jackson, Michigan (c.205 mi), split by opening piece and operator: Cincinnati, Van Wert & Michigan (1881 - Mar 1886), Cincinnati, Jackson & Mackinaw (Mar 1886 - 23 Jul 1897), Cincinnati Northern (23 Jul 1897 - 31 Jan 1930), Big Four / NYC Northern Division (1 Feb 1930 - 1936 north of Van Wert, 1938 south). Also the 1896-1901 CJ&M/CN through trains to Cincinnati Court Street over the Big Four, M&C and CL&N. Research report: research/branches/cincinnati_northern_railroad.txt.

geometry_sources: OpenStreetMap (Overpass, maps.mail.ru mirror, 2026-10-29): old_railway_operator probed in the corridor - the road is tagged only 'NYC' (no 'CN', 'Cincinnati Northern', 'Big Four' or 'CCC&StL' spelling; one way named 'Cincinnati Northern'); NYC-tagged Dupps Railroad, Franklin Industrial Track, Celina-Coldwater Bikeway and abandoned grade; untagged rail into Jackson; Indiana & Ohio Mason Subdivision.

OpenHistoricalMap (2026-10-29): 'Cincinnati, Jackson and Mackinaw Railroad' ways (Jackson - Addison Junction - Bryan, Cecil - Van Wert area), 'Spencerville and Elgin Railroad', 'Middletown & Cincinnati Railroad', 'Cincinnati, Lebanon & Northern Railway' (Court Street approach), and untagged OHM railway ways (CL&N south of Mason). Addison Junction is the OHM node where the CJ&M and DT&M ways meet (41.9928,-84.3288).

Routed with opstrace.py (douglas_peucker 8 m, trim_reversals). Nominatim geocodes checked by type; hand-pinned: Jackson (Amtrak/MC station; Nominatim gave Jackson County), Paulding and Van Wert (gave the counties), Ohio City (gave Cleveland's neighbourhood), Addison Junction, Carlisle Junction, Franklin, Hageman (Nominatim gave a Shelby County hamlet), Court Street station. Furnace, Flat Rock, Folmer and Clarks Lake geocoded to wrong places and were dropped as waypoints.
metadata.operator_split: Rule 4 splits at: Mar 1886 CVW&M -> CJ&M (consolidation); 23 Jul 1897 CJ&M (receiver) -> Cincinnati Northern (foreclosure purchase); 1 Feb 1930 Cincinnati Northern -> Big Four (99-year lease). NOT splits: the 1892 CJ&M Railroad -> Railway reorganisation (same name), Big Four stock control from 1902 (CN ran its own trains to 1917, ICC), USRA 1918-1920, the 30 Jun 1938 merger (after the last passenger train). Split features share identical geometry for the same piece. NB the CL&N's own 1881-1883 predecessor was also called 'Cincinnati Northern Railway' (a TD&B subsidiary) - a DIFFERENT company from the 1894-1938 Cincinnati Northern Railroad drawn here; do not merge their colours.
metadata.colors: Big Four colour pulled programmatically from the existing 'Cleveland, Cincinnati, Chicago and St. Louis Railway' features. CVW&M, CJ&M and Cincinnati Northern are new companies: colours chosen by script as the hex furthest from every colour already in data/ within amber, green and crimson hue bands, so the three eras read as distinct.
metadata.freight_only_audit: Nothing freight-only drawn. Excluded: Lewisburg quarry branch (1.1 mi, freight); all post-passenger freight years (Van Wert - Jackson 1936 -> 1975/77, Van Wert - Franklin 1938 -> 1977-82); post-1976 short lines (Western Ohio, Spencerville & Elgin, R.J. Corman, Chicago Ft. Wayne & Eastern, Pioneer).
metadata.horsecar_audit: None: every predecessor was a steam railroad from opening.
not_yet_sourced: Report blocks [14] (CJ&M operation of the Michigan & Ohio, Addison Jct - Battle Creek, 1888 [ANCHOR]) and [15] (DT&M under Cincinnati Northern lease, Addison Jct - Marshall, 1899 [ANCHOR]; lease 1 Feb 1899 - 1 Jan 1902 per CNMRRC-H vs michiganrailroads' 1899 lease then MC/LS&MS 1905) are NOT drawn here - single-year anchors on Michigan & Ohio / DT&M track, left for a DT&M research pass so that line is drawn by its own owner first.

Not drawn (drawable NONE): [9] narrow-gauge Columbus & North Western era Van Wert - Rockford 1879-1881 (no passenger evidence); [10] Paulding & Cecil independent era 1880-c.1881 (operator unknown); [11] CJ&M trains Carlisle - Cincinnati over the CH&D 1888-1896 (rights documented, trains not); [13] CN trains Franklin Jct - Cincinnati over the Big Four after 1901 (contract only; CNMRRC says the last trains ran only to Middletown, Fowler annotates Franklin '(operated over CCCStL to:) Cincinnati (Union Terminal)' - conflict).
The 1 Feb 1938 end south of Van Wert rests on one source (CNMRRC brief history); a Feb 1938 Official Guide would settle it.
West Alexandria - Carlisle 1888 start is weak (no timetable names these stations before the CN era).
Van Wert - Rockford start 1881 is the earliest confirmed year [OPEN start], not a known opening of passenger service; Paulding & Cecil opening is in conflict (1877/1880/1884/1885).
Operator of Addison Jct - Jackson 5 Jan 1897 - 1 Jun 1898 'not ascertained' (ICC); the HS98 card date OCRs as 1897 or 1898.
Every headway_min and avg_speed_kmh is an estimate from train counts, not a timetable reading.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced 18.8 mi against 18.7 mi (ICC; Fowler 18.8) plus 1.22 mi of Michigan Central track into Jackson. Jackson end: the CJ&M/CN own line is OpenHistoricalMap 'Cincinnati, Jackson and Mackinaw Railroad' (start_date 1896) to its north end at 42.2379,-84.3931; the last 1.0 mi traced (1.22 mi per ICC) into the Michigan Central / Amtrak station is on untagged present-day yard and spur track of ANOTHER COMPANY (the MC/NYC), used under a contract of 19 Aug 1907 - the pre-1907 arrangement into Jackson was not found, so for 1898-1907 that last mile is the later-documented approach. Traced along the road's own grade: OSM ways tagged old_railway_operator=NYC (Dupps Railroad, Franklin Industrial Track, Celina-Coldwater Bikeway, abandoned grade) and OpenHistoricalMap 'Cincinnati, Jackson and Mackinaw Railroad' ways (Jackson - Addison Jct - Bryan, Cecil - Van Wert), 2.0 mi of OHM 'Spencerville and Elgin Railroad' near Ohio City (the same track, re-used by the S&E from 1978). Whole main line 203.8 mi traced (Jackson CJ&M connection - Franklin) against 205.4 mi by Fowler's chainage. Every waypoint town lies within 0.9 km of the drawn line. No straight-line legs.

segments.note: Addison Junction - Cement City - Clarks Lake - Jackson (Jackson & Cincinnati Ry, built 1896, conveyed to the CN 1 Jun 1898). Opened 1896 and run by the CJ&M to 5 Jan 1897, then by an operator the ICC 'not ascertained' until 1 Jun 1898 - so the CJ&M years 1896-97 are NOT drawn. First confirmed passenger year 1898: Cincinnati Northern Time-Table No. 5 (Hillsdale Standard 23 Aug 1898) names 'Cincinnati and Jackson Mail' trains. Cement City (as Woodstock) in the 1900 Guide (Fowler). Three trains each way until 1927 (michiganrailroads). Cincinnati Northern era: bought the CJ&M Ohio Division at foreclosure 23 Jul 1897 and the Jackson & Cincinnati 1 Jun 1898; operated 'by its own organization' to 31 Dec 1917 although the Big Four held stock control from 1 Jan 1902 (ICC - not an operator change); USRA federal control 1 Jan 1918 - 29 Feb 1920 (wartime, not drawn as a split); leased to the Big Four from 1 Feb 1930, where this feature ends. headway_min is an estimate from the stated train counts, not a timetable reading.
sources: Segment-level: 1898 from the CN timetable printed Aug 1898 (HS98); operators and dates from the ICC valuation; frequency from MRR-T36.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced 43.2 mi against c.42 mi: c.6 mi Big Four Franklin - Middletown (not established), M&C Middletown - Hageman (part of the 14.1-mi M&C; not separately established), c.24.9 mi CL&N Hageman - Court Street (Fowler line 86). ENTIRELY ON OTHER COMPANIES' TRACK (trackage rights): 6.7 mi Big Four (Cincinnati - Dayton line, today's NYC-tagged Franklin Industrial Track and abandoned grade) Franklin - Middletown; 11.8 mi Middletown & Cincinnati (OHM 'Middletown & Cincinnati Railroad' and the Indiana & Ohio Mason Subdivision) Middletown - Hageman; 24.7 mi CL&N Hageman - Mason - Deer Park - Norwood - Court Street (I&O Mason Subdivision, untagged OSM and OpenHistoricalMap ways incl. OHM 'Cincinnati, Lebanon & Northern Railway' through the Walnut Hills tunnel to Court Street) against 24.9 mi documented. No straight-line legs. Hageman is placed at the present Mason Sub / Lebanon Sub junction (39.389,-84.270) and Court Street at the OHM CL&N terminus (39.106,-84.505); Middletown waypoint lies 1.1 km from the drawn line (town centre). The Big Four - M&C connection at Middletown is the router's choice and was not checked against an 1896 map.

segments.note: The CJ&M's Court Street expresses continued under the Cincinnati Northern over the Big Four, the Middletown & Cincinnati and the CL&N: Time-Table No. 5 (1897/98) names 'Cincinnati and Jackson Mail' trains. The CN 'terminated its use of the CL&N in 1901' (Wikipedia / Hauck, via the CL&N research file); the replacement Big Four trackage contract is dated 1 Mar 1901 (ICC). After 1901 where CN trains terminated in the south is unresolved and is NOT drawn (report block [13]). headway_min is an estimate from the stated train counts, not a timetable reading.
sources: Segment-level: 1897 = CN purchase (ICC); trains confirmed by HS98; 1901 end from Wikipedia/Hauck and the 1 Mar 1901 Big Four contract (ICC).

Traced along the road's own grade: OSM ways tagged old_railway_operator=NYC (Dupps Railroad, Franklin Industrial Track, Celina-Coldwater Bikeway, abandoned grade) and OpenHistoricalMap 'Cincinnati, Jackson and Mackinaw Railroad' ways (Jackson - Addison Jct - Bryan, Cecil - Van Wert), 2.0 mi of OHM 'Spencerville and Elgin Railroad' near Ohio City (the same track, re-used by the S&E from 1978). Whole main line 203.8 mi traced (Jackson CJ&M connection - Franklin) against 205.4 mi by Fowler's chainage. Every waypoint town lies within 0.9 km of the drawn line. No straight-line legs. Franklin end: the CN met the Big Four (Cincinnati - Dayton line, today's NYC-tagged Franklin Industrial Track) near 39.576,-84.320 and the drawn line runs c.1 mi south on Big Four track to end in Franklin (joint station from 1 Dec 1914, ICC); the exact depot site was not located. The 1936-1938 trains ran on to Middletown over Big Four track; that Franklin - Middletown leg is not drawn as a separate feature (no confirmed year for CN/Big Four Northern Division trains on it beyond the CNMRRC phrase; Big Four's own layer covers the track).

segments.note: Big Four era: the Cincinnati Northern was leased to the Cleveland, Cincinnati, Chicago and St. Louis (Big Four, itself leased to the New York Central) for 99 years from 1 Feb 1930 and run as its Northern Division ([ICC]); merged 30 Jun 1938, after the last passenger train. Van Wert - Celina - Greenville - Lewisburg - Carlisle - Franklin, the service lasting '22 months longer' than north of Van Wert. Passenger service south of Van Wert ended 1 Feb 1938 - the last trains ran 'south to Middletown' - per the CNMRRC brief history ONLY; CNMRRC notes agree on the year at Lewisburg ('all passenger service ended in 1938'). SINGLE-SOURCE END: a Feb 1938 Official Guide or a local 'last train' story would confirm it. Freight continued into the 1970s-80s. headway_min is an estimate from the stated train counts, not a timetable reading.
sources: Segment-level: 1930 start = Big Four lease (ICC); 1 Feb 1938 end from the CNMRRC brief history ONLY (single source), year agreed by CNMRRC notes.
